Throughout the Bible, righteousness is often portrayed as a key attribute of God and a desired quality for believers. It is linked to peace, salvation, and the prosperity of the land. In Psalm 85, righteousness is portrayed as meeting with love, faithfulness, and peace, and prepares the way for God's steps. This symbol develops throughout the Bible as a central theme in God's character and His expectations for His people.
Symbols2Summarize: The most important symbol in these verses that recurs throughout the Bible is the altar. The altar represents worship, sacrifice, and the presence of God. In this passage, Elijah repairs the altar of the Lord and offers a sacrifice to demonstrate God's power. Throughout the Bible, altars are used by the patriarchs and prophets as a place of worship and connection with God. They are seen as a central symbol of faith and devotion to God.
Symbols3Summarize: The most important symbol in these verses that recurs throughout the Bible is the Scriptures. Apollos is described as having a thorough knowledge of the Scriptures and he uses them to accurately teach about Jesus. He is able to refute his Jewish opponents by proving from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Messiah. This highlights the importance of the Scriptures as a source of divine revelation and guidance.
Summarize1: God promises peace to his faithful servants who listen to Him and avoid folly. Salvation is near those who fear Him, bringing glory to the land. Love, faithfulness, righteousness, and peace complement each other. The Lord will give good things and blessings to the land. Righteousness clears the path for His steps.
Summarize2: In this passage, Elijah confronts King Ahab and the prophets of Baal. He challenges them to a test to determine who is the true God. Elijah repairs the Lord's altar and pours water on the sacrifice three times. He prays to God, and fire comes down and consumes the sacrifice, wood, stones, and water. The people recognize the Lord as the true God and Elijah has the prophets of Baal killed.
Summarize3: Apollos, a knowledgeable Jew from Alexandria, came to Ephesus and taught about Jesus accurately. Priscilla and Aquila invited him to their home and explained more about God to him. Apollos then went to Achaia with the encouragement of the believers, where he vigorously debated and proved that Jesus was the Messiah, using the Scriptures.
Behindinsights1: An interesting insight from external research is that Psalm 85 is considered a psalm of lament. It is believed to have been written during a time of national crisis or distress, possibly during the Babylonian exile. This adds additional context and significance to the themes of peace, salvation, and righteousness mentioned in the passage.
Behindinsights3: One interesting insight is that Apollos was from Alexandria, which was a renowned center of learning in the ancient world. As a learned man, it is likely that he had a strong education in Greek philosophy and rhetoric, which would have made him an effective and persuasive speaker. This could explain why he spoke with great fervor and was able to refute his opponents in public debate (Acts 18:25-28).
